title: Responses adapter spec and canary rollout plan for OpenAI Responses API parity
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Background: Customers using the OpenAI Responses API expect a specific set of behaviors for streaming semantics, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. We need an adapter layer that translates between Redwood's native Responses model and the OpenAI Responses wire semantics with minimal latency and robust correctness.

Scope:
- Implement a request/response adapter that maps Redwood request fields to OpenAI-compatible request shapes and back.
- Streaming translator: convert Redwood streaming deltas into OpenAI-compatible event chunks and finish_reason mappings.
- Tool/function calling translation: support both explicit 'tool' outputs and function call-style interactions, including partial tool output streaming and final tool completion events.
- Structured output enforcement: validate/serialize content when callers request schema-constrained outputs (json_schema/schemaHints).
- Interop test harness and canary rollout (per-customer opt-in + 1% global).

Non-goals: full parity for historic OpenAI edge cases (we'll document incompatibilities); rewriting runtime core — adapter should be a lightweight layer.

Compatibility matrix (high level):
- Streaming: map Redwood 'chunk' events to OpenAI 'delta' tokens; preserve role attribution and ensure consistent finish_reason mapping. Handle mid-stream tool output and resume semantics.
- Finish reasons: Redwood 'cancelled' and 'context_truncated' -> OpenAI 'stop' or 'length' with metadata in event payloads.
- Tool calling: Redwood tool outputs that arrive as streamed binary blobs must be chunked and emitted as tool events; final tool call must include return_value type, name, and metadata.
- Structured outputs: when schema provided, adapter must run a permissive validator and emit 'structured_output' events even when validation fails (with error annotations) rather than silently coercing.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Automated interop tests covering streaming text-only, streaming with tool output, function-call-first-turn, nested structured outputs, and intentional validation failures.
2) End-to-end performance: adapter adds <=5% median latency at 95th percentile under our benchmark workload.
3) Canary rollout with telemetry: 1% traffic for 48h, expand to 10% if no regressions.
4) Documentation: public API compatibility notes + examples and migration guide.

Technical approach: lightweight adapter implemented as a separate service process in front of the runtime router. Components: request normalizer, streaming event projector, tool-call broker, structured-output validator. Prefer zero-copy streaming when possible; where not possible, batch small chunks to avoid socket thrash.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Pros: isolates translation logic, easier to iterate on mapping rules.
- Cons: extra hop risks added latency and increased operational surface area; must guard with strict timeouts and circuit breakers.
- Edge-case risk: third-party client libraries that rely on undocumented stream ordering may break. We'll capture these as known incompatibilities.

Migration plan:
- Stage 1: internal test harness + compatibility matrix validation (this ticket).
- Stage 2: opt-in canary by customer flag; collect mismatch metrics and error rates.
- Stage 3: wider rollout with documented breaking changes and a migration checklist for customers.

Rollout playbook:
- Day 0: deploy adapter to internal staging and run fuzz tests.
- Day 1: enable 1% canary with telemetry capture (errors, finish_reason mismatches, validation failures).
- Day 3: review telemetry and fix critical mismatches.
- Day 7: expand to 10% if stable; announce docs and examples.

Monitoring & test plan: telemetry tags for adapter-version, mapping-rule-id, stream-latency-ms, validation-failures, tool-call-time-ms. Create dashboards in Console: 'adapter-errors', 'adapter-latency-p50-p95', 'compat-mismatch-count'.

Documentation links: add 'compatibility notes' doc and migration guide to Confluence and public docs repo.
comments: 2025-02-12 Sofia Nguyen: Created initial draft of adapter spec after whiteboard session with Runtime and SDK teams. Prioritized streaming semantics and tool-calling cases.

2025-02-14 Carlos Medina: Completed first-pass streaming event projector prototype. Verified conversion of Redwood 'kv_cache' metadata to an OpenAI-compatible 'metadata' field. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1923

2025-02-18 Lydia Park (SDK): Found discrepancy where OpenAI clients expect role changes mid-stream to be a separate event. Added test vector and updated mapping rules to emit explicit role-change deltas.

2025-02-20 Rodrigo Alves (QA): Ran interop tests with open-source OpenAI-client fuzzer. Observed two classes of mismatch: finish_reason mapping for cancelled streams, and partial tool output chunk ordering. Filed follow-ups ENG-10027 and ENG-10028.

2025-02-24 Carlos Medina: Benchmarks on staging show adapter adds 3.8% median latency and 6.1% p95 under the standard token mix. Under heavy tool-output streaming, p95 increased to 9.4% — will investigate batching heuristics.
2025-02-26 Sofia Nguyen: Updated acceptance criteria and canary plan after perf run. Security review requested (KMS interaction for tool payloads).
notes: Priority coordinated with PM; sensitive to latency and incorrect tool-call semantics. Security review in progress for tool payload KMS handling.
